hook_text: Same bar, same brick. Slide the brick and the lever makes you stronger, the same, or weaker.
clip_script: A bar, a brick and a loose paving slab. Brick close to the slab: a gentle push lifts it. Mechanical advantage above 1. Brick in the exact middle: you push with the same force as the slab's weight, you just push down instead of lifting up. Advantage of 1, like a seesaw with two equal children. Brick close to your hands: now you strain, but the slab end flies up fast and far. Advantage below 1. That is a first-class lever, the only kind with the pivot in the middle, and the only kind that can do all three. Scissors are two of them joined at the screw. A pedal bin is one: foot down, lid up. A rescue spreader is one: pivot near the tips, so a hydraulic push becomes a crushing grip. Rule to keep: the longer side carries the smaller force.
visual_style: Whiteboard bar over a brick; the brick slides left, centre, right while the effort arrow shrinks and grows and the slab end rises by different amounts.
mood: Playful experiment, three quick outcomes from one move.
pacing: Three fast demonstrations, then three everyday examples, then the one-line rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find the pivot on a pair of scissors and a seesaw.
